_about: Barnaby for ElevenLabs v4, performed as passages (one request per scene, split by the alignment) so his voice stays one voice. Sparse direction: punctuation carries the rhythm; a tag only where it changes the read. Same words as cues.json.
06: Twenty-three endpoints, sir. I've taken the six that only read — nobody's given me any keys yet.
12: Five bikes due tomorrow. Only Anika's is a problem — her brakes need two pairs of pads, and we've one left.
14: I can't order parts myself yet — but Theo built the system a way to. Shall I take that on?
16: Ten pairs from Madison, at six pounds fifty a pair. Shall I?
19: I'll need to text her and mark it ready... May I?
23: That's three bikes handed back, and the same four steps each time. Shall I make it one?
27: Tom's been texted, and it's marked ready.
29: The system can't tell me — there's no report for it. [brightly, matter-of-fact] Theo always meant to write one.
30: [lightly] I could write it... if you like.
32: With your say-so. I'll work on a copy — nothing changes until you've seen it.
33: Done. It adds up each mechanic's hours, the way Theo's notes count them. It only reads, and all of Theo's checks still pass. Shall I add it?
35: That one needs your click, Martin... I don't change the system on a word.
37: Dev's carrying thirty-one hours against his twenty. Priya starts tomorrow — shall I give her the two wheel builds?
40: [wryly, a little cheeky] Guilty. Dev had thirty-one hours booked. You had none.
42: Your jobs, the parts they need, who's collecting what. And Theo left you a note: [amused] never trust the stock count on a Friday.
45: Thirteen endpoints, sir — and two deadlines in dispute. Shall I flag them?
49: Twenty-eight endpoints. It's on the big card, and three jobs are queued.
